title: A general-purpose self-supervised model for computational pathology
study_context: Large-scale self-supervised pathology representation learning; downloaded source is the author preprint.
population_or_data: More than 100 million patches from more than 100,000 diagnostic H&E WSIs across 20 major tissue types.
task: Transfer general pathology representations to ROI- and slide-level tasks.
method: Self-supervised vision-transformer encoder followed by task-specific probing or MIL aggregation.
main_findings: UNI was pretrained at substantially larger pathology scale than prior general-purpose encoders in the paper.
Slide-level use first extracts patch features and then trains an aggregation model such as ABMIL.
limitations: Pretraining is centered on diagnostic H&E and does not directly test this project's cardiac, stain, magnification, or scanner combinations.
does_not_establish: The publication does not establish that UNI or UNI2-h is the best encoder for local cardiac allograft images.
relevance_to_project: Strong encoder candidate whose value must be established by local ablation and held-out evaluation.
